Did a dog really wait nine years for his owner?
A professor named Hidesaburo Ueno adopted a fluffy Akita puppy.
Every evening, Hachiko waited for him at Shibuya Station.
The next evening, he went to the station.
For nine years and nine months...
he showed up right when the train arrived.
At first, people shooed him away.
Then a newspaper told his story...
and all of Japan fell in love with him.
In 1934, they built him a bronze statue.
And Hachiko was there to see it.
Only in March 1935, when he passed away.
Today, part of his remains rest beside the professor's grave.
